name: CA-50
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Scott Peters holds a D+10 district with a large cash advantage
Challenger Steve Cohen shows no reported fundraising or outside support
No general-election polling; forecast rests on district fundamentals
Prediction markets price Peters near 95% to win
model.rationale: Peters combines a D+10 seat, incumbency, and a roughly $2.6 million warhead of cash on hand against a challenger with no visible fundraising, and markets price him around 95% to win. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending for Cohen or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race would be the first sign this is closer than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Peters, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He enters the general election with roughly $2.6 million in cash on hand after raising about $1.8 million, while Republican Steve Cohen reports no fundraising and draws no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets price Peters at about a 95% chance of winning.

No public general-election polling is available for this race, so expectations rest on the district's partisan lean, Peters's incumbency advantage, and the lopsided financial picture. The combination points to a comfortable double-digit win for Peters, with the seat firmly in Democratic hands absent an unexpected shift in the race's fundamentals.
